basic: Trigger plus five clean, well-separated hits (centre, off-centre, near edges).
ambiguous_x2: x1 with 2-3 x2 candidates: first in search order kept (how_many_x==~1 quirk); first-found x2 wrong -> hit dropped, the other x2 never retried; -1 before +1.
ambiguous_y: Two valid y pairs (first in nested y1/y2 search order kept), a y1 with no partner before one with, one y1 with two y2; `break` leaves only the y2 loop.
tol_x_window: |x1-x2| = 3198, 3200 (kept: skip is > T_sum), 3202, 3300, 3398 (dropped by the T_sum skip although < 3400), and -3200/-3202.
tol_y_diff: |y1-y2| = 3398 kept, 3400/3402 dropped (strict <3400); a y1 exactly 3200 bins from x1 kept, 3201 skipped though the pair is consistent (the window is relative to x1).
tol_sum: x sum - y sum = 398 kept, 400 and 402 dropped, -398 kept, -400 dropped, 400 and 398 with sx != 3200 (T then uses T_sum, not the real sums).
dead_time_x1: x1 pulses 15000/20000/20001/19999 bins apart and two at the same time, each with its own partners: 2019 matches all; 2023's uniquetol keeps the first of each 20000-bin group (not chained, inclusive), ties keep the first row.
empty: A 0-byte file: MATLAB errors at t_zero = dld_output_raw(1,2).
blank_only: A file holding one CRLF: textscan gives 0 rows; MATLAB errors as for empty.
trigger_only: One trigger row: no hits (2019 writes no file; 2023 an empty one).
no_hits: Trigger plus corner pulses that never form a hit: x1 with no x2, x2/y alone.
phantom_lone_pair: Trigger + x1 + x2 and no y: NaN(floor(3/4)=0,5) grows with ZEROS when the x pair is stored, so the failed row keeps T=0 and survives the NaN filter: a hit at T=0, Y=0.
phantom_after_hit: Trigger + one hit + a lone x pair after it (N=7, prealloc 1 row): the lone pair grows row 2 with zeros -> a phantom T=0 row.
phantom_none: Same as phantom_after_hit but the lone pair comes BEFORE the hit: the row is reused by the hit, no phantom.
phantom_multi: Trigger + 3 hits + x1,x2,y1 (N=16, prealloc 4 rows, 3 successes): row 4 is preallocated NaN, so no phantom (contrast with phantom_after_hit).
phantom_multi_cut: phantom_multi without the lone y1 (N=15, prealloc 3, 3 successes): the lone pair grows row 4 with zeros -> a phantom T=0 row.
no_trailing_newline: Two hits, last line without CRLF.
lf_endings: Two hits with LF line endings.
blank_lines: Two hits with blank lines in the middle and at the end (textscan skips them).
trunc_digits: Last line cut mid-number (still being written): its time loses digits, sorts to near the trigger, and the last hit loses a pulse.
trunc_comma: Last line is '<ch>,' (time missing): textscan gives NaN, which sorts last.
trunc_channel: Last line is '<ch>' only: textscan gives (ch, NaN).
trunc_cr: Last line ends in a lone CR.
nan_time_mid: A line '0' (no time) in the middle: (0, NaN) sorts last and counts in N.
garbage_mid: A non-numeric line in the middle: textscan (ReturnOnError) stops there, so only the rows before it are read.
tzero_nan: The first line is '5,' (no time): t_zero is NaN, every time becomes NaN, no hits.
hits_at_edges: A hit before the trigger (negative T) whose x2 is the first sorted row (reachable at count+dummy = 1), and a hit whose x1 is the last row (search runs past N).
first_sorted_x1: The earliest pulse is an x1 (before the trigger): sorted row 1 is skipped as 'the trigger' though it is a corner, so its hit is lost.
unsorted: Trigger first, then pulses in shuffled order including five earlier channel-5 rows: t_zero is row 1 (the trigger), not the minimum.
tzero_not_trigger: The first line is a corner pulse (x2 of hit 2), the trigger second: t_zero is that pulse's time, so every T shifts by it (some T negative).
equal_times: Pulses at identical times (stable sort keeps file order), two hits with equal T (final sort is stable), and hits generated out of T order (final sort reorders).
search_window: An x2 > T_sum away inside the 36-row window is skipped and the search goes on; partners at row +-19 are out of reach, at +-18 found (offsets -1,+1,...,-18,+18).
used_pulses: Two x1 sharing one x2 (the first takes it; the pulse is then NaN for the second); an x2 whose x1 found no y stays free for the next x1.
mcp_present: Four hits each with an MCP (channel 4) pulse: MCP rows sit in the window but are ignored.
mcp_absent: The same four hits without MCP pulses (output must equal mcp_present's).
other_channels: Channels 6 and 7 among the hits (ignored, but occupy window rows).
small_values: Hits ~25 ns to 0.5 us after the trigger and |X|,|Y| of a few bins: T and X/Y print with e-05/e-06/e-07 exponents; X or Y exactly 0; odd sums give quarter-bin T.
large_times: Hits at 0.1, 1.0, 2.0 and 10 s after the trigger: T >= 1 prints 8 significant digits (rounding at the 8th digit), quarter bins.
trigger_burst: Twelve channel-5 rows within 1 us of the trigger (as in 2024-11 d1111) and hits starting 50 ns later, inside the trigger rows' window.
